questions.question: 1. Differential protection should be provided in the transformers whose rating:

explanations.a: Correct. Differential protection is typically provided for transformers rated above 5 MVA as per IEEE/IEC standards.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Smaller transformers (below 5 MVA) usually use fuses or overcurrent protection.
explanations.c: Incorrect. 50 MVA is too high a threshold; differential protection is needed above 5 MVA.

questions.question: 2. The differential protection of transformer does not cover the following fault:

answers.c: Inter turn fault in any winding
answers.d: Short circuit faults at transformer bushing

explanations.a: Incorrect. Winding to ground faults are covered if they cause current difference.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Winding to winding (phase to phase) faults are covered.
explanations.c: Correct. Small inter-turn faults may not produce sufficient differential current as the turns ratio change is small.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Bushing faults are in the protected zone if CTs are on both sides of bushings.

questions.question: 3. Which type of connection is employed for current transformers for the protection of Delta-Star connected 3-phase transformer:

explanations.a: Incorrect. Delta-Star for CTs would not correct the phase shift.
explanations.b: Correct. For a Delta-Star power transformer, CTs are connected in Star on the delta side and Delta on the star side to compensate for 30° phase shift.

questions.question: 4. Which Differential protection principle is used in the protection of transformer:

explanations.a: Correct. Differential protection compares the difference between primary and secondary currents (after magnitude and phase correction).
explanations.b: Incorrect. Voltage difference is not used for transformer differential protection.

questions.question: 5. In differential protection of transformer the CTs on both side of transformer are:

answers.b: Their turns ratio has inverse relation
answers.c: Their turns ratio has no relationship

explanations.a: Incorrect. CTs cannot be identical because primary currents on HV and LV sides are different.
explanations.b: Correct. CT turns ratio is inversely proportional to the transformer voltage ratio so that secondary currents are balanced.
explanations.c: Incorrect. There is a definite relationship.
